newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Swiss Life (Belgium) 1996 profit 190 to 200 mln Bfr.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Life (Belgium) 1996 profit 190 to 200 mln Bfr.

text.p: Swiss Life's Swiss Life (Belgium) unit said on Wednesday it had a 1996 net profit of between 190 and 200 million Belgian francs compared with 127 million francs a year earlier.
"In terms of profit, it looks very nice...it will be between 190 and 200 million,", said Louis Durieux, who takes over from Jean-Pierre Troussel as Swiss Life (Belgium) Director General on March 1.

Swiss Life (Belgium), one of the 10 leading life insurers in Belgium and the largest foreign life insurer in Belgium, bought a 37.45 percent stake in Belgian Credit Agricole/Landbouwkrediet (INCA/NILK) from the Belgian state in 1995.
In November 1996, it bought 100 percent of French insurer GAN's GAN Belgium unit for 3.5 billion Belgian francs.
Durieux said that GAN Belgium had a profit of about 200 million francs in 1996 plus 200 million francs in capital gains.
He added that GAN Belgium's profit would not be consolidated in 1996, but only from 1997.
Durieux told a news conference that premium income of Swiss Life (Belgium) was between 5.9 and 6.0 billion francs in 1996, compared with 5.7 billion francs in 1995.

"We're still very satisfied with this because we had been expecting a certain decrease in income just due to the fact that for an important contract we had to allow co-insurance...which meant that between 500 million and one billion in premium income disappeared," Durieux said.
"We were able to compensate this nicely with internal growth," he added.
Companies account for 45 percent of Swiss Life (Belgium)'s clients, pension funds for 30 percent and retail clients for 25 percent.
Swiss Life (Belgium), formed in 1955, has a workforce of 274.
